heading.en: Telling the chip what to do

hook.en: A program is a recipe: fetch this, add that, store the answer, stop. Today we write real 8085 *programs*, trace them byte by byte and even make the processor wait for an exact time.

title.en: Write programs to add and subtract 8-bit numbers stored in memory
Handle the carry with conditional jumps
Calculate the delay produced by a counter loop

say.en: A program is a recipe: fetch this, add that, store the answer, stop. Today we write real 8085 programs, trace them byte by byte and even make the processor wait for an exact time. In this lesson: Write programs to add and subtract 8-bit numbers stored in memory.
Handle the carry with conditional jumps.
Calculate the delay produced by a counter loop.

body.en: Steps: state the problem, draw a flowchart, write the mnemonics, then hand-assemble them into hexadecimal opcodes at chosen memory addresses. Example: add two 8-bit numbers at 2050H and 2051H and store the sum at 2052H: LXI H, 2050H; MOV A, M; INX H; ADD M; STA 2052H; HLT. To keep the carry, clear a register (MVI C, 00H) before the addition and use JNC to skip INR C when there is no carry. Subtraction uses SUB M in the same way; the carry flag then shows a borrow.

title.en: Counting the time of a delay loop

narration.en: MVI C loads the count once (7 T). Each pass through the loop runs DCR C (4 T) and JNZ (10 T when it jumps back, 7 T on the last pass). Step through the loop and watch C fall and the T-states add up to 14N + 4.
narration.kn: MVI C ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಎಣಿಕೆ ತುಂಬುತ್ತದೆ (7 T). ಪ್ರತಿ ಕುಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ DCR C (4 T) ಮತ್ತು JNZ (ಹಿಂದೆ ಜಿಗಿದರೆ 10 T, ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ 7 T). ಒಟ್ಟು 14N + 4.

say.kn: MVI C ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಎಣಿಕೆ ತುಂಬುತ್ತದೆ 7 T. ಪ್ರತಿ ಕುಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ DCR C 4 T ಮತ್ತು JNZ (ಹಿಂದೆ ಜಿಗಿದರೆ 10 T, ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ 7 T). ಒಟ್ಟು 14 newtons plus 4.

body.en: A loop repeats instructions using a counter register and a conditional jump. A delay loop wastes a known time: MVI C, N (7 T-states); LOOP: DCR C (4 T); JNZ LOOP (10 T when it jumps, 7 T when it does not). The total is $T = 7 + 4N + 10(N - 1) + 7 = 14N + 4$ T-states, and the delay is this number multiplied by the T-state time. With N = FFH = 255 at 3 MHz, 3574 × 0.333 µs ≈ 1.19 ms.

points.en: DCR C sets Z = 1 when C reaches 0

narration.en: A delay loop counts a register down to zero. Each pass costs fourteen T-states, so the delay is fourteen N plus four T-states times the clock period.

problem.en: Write a program to add the numbers at 2050H and 2051H, store the sum at 2052H and the carry at 2053H. Trace it for 9AH and 89H.

steps.en: LDA 2050H; MOV B, A; LDA 2051H; MVI C, 00H
ADD B; JNC SKIP; INR C
SKIP: STA 2052H; MOV A, C; STA 2053H; HLT

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Write a program to add the numbers at 2050H and 2051H, store the sum at 2052H and the carry at 2053H. Trace it for 9AH and 89H.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Write a program to add the numbers at 2050H and 2051H, store the sum at 2052H and the carry at 2053H. Trace it for 9AH and 89H.
LDA 2050H; MOV B, A; LDA 2051H; MVI C, 00H.
ADD B; JNC SKIP; INR C.
SKIP: STA 2052H; MOV A, C; STA 2053H; HLT.
Trace: 9AH plus 89H equals 123H gives 2052H equals 23H; CY equals 1 so C equals 01H gives 2053H equals 01H.
So the answer is 2052H equals 23H, 2053H equals 01H.

problem.en: A delay loop uses MVI C, 64H (N = 100) with DCR C and JNZ at an operating frequency of 3 MHz. Find the delay.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A delay loop uses MVI C, 64H (N = 100) with DCR C and JNZ at an operating frequency of 3 MHz. Find the delay.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A delay loop uses MVI C, 64H N equals 100 with DCR C and JNZ at an operating frequency of 3 megahertz. Find the delay.
T-states equals 14 newtons plus 4 equals 14 times 100 plus 4 equals 1404.
T-state time equals 1 over 3 megahertz is approximately 0.333 microseconds.
Delay equals 1404 divided by 3 microseconds equals 468 microseconds.
So the answer is 468 microseconds.
